title: Meta-Judging with Large Language Models: Concepts, Methods, and Challenges

bias_targets.methodology: Swapping the order of candidate responses or judgments during pairwise comparisons to detect if the evaluator systematically favors the first or second presented option, and testing consistency across varying judge pool sizes.
Applying length-controlled preference selection and measuring if the meta-judge disproportionately favors longer outputs when the underlying quality or scores are similar.
Assessing whether an LLM evaluator exhibits a tendency to assign higher scores to text or responses that it generated itself compared to responses generated by other models.
Using simplified multi-agent frameworks to test whether an evaluating agent unjustifiably aligns its judgments with the perceived majority or prior referee evaluations.
Isolating bias effects in controlled evaluation environments to determine if LLM judges inherently favor responses formatted with step-by-step reasoning structures regardless of actual correctness.
Analyzing the distribution of assigned scores to detect a tendency of the judging system to over-assign high scores or favor responses that appear overly confident, leading to score saturation.
